sources.title: Sweden sees rare fall in air passengers, as flight-shaming takes off (10 January 2020)
sources.license: BBC terms of use, all rights reserved (facts only)
sources.note: 引用瑞典機場營運單位 Swedavia 的 2019 年統計

facts.text: In 2013 and 2014 night train lines such as Paris–Madrid, Berlin–Paris and Amsterdam–Prague were cut.
Night trains lost passengers to low-cost airlines, cars, buses and high-speed trains, and there was little investment in new carriages.
Night trains are expensive to run: they need special carriages, usually make one journey a day and gain few passengers at stops in the middle of the night.
Austria’s national railway ÖBB took over many night routes abandoned by Germany’s Deutsche Bahn, including Munich–Rome.
The flygskam (flight shame) movement spread from Scandinavia and encourages people to choose alternatives to flying.
In 2019 the number of domestic air passengers in Sweden fell by 9 percent, according to the airport operator Swedavia.
facts.note: 更正（2026-10-09 fact_check）：原本寫成 2018 年（照抄 CNN 2020-12-14 的說法）。Swedavia 年度統計：2018 年國內旅客 13,542,000 人，只比 2017 年少約 3%；約 9% 的降幅在 2019 年（BBC 2020-01-10 引 Swedavia）

facts.text: The European Union designated 2021 the European Year of Rail.
New night routes and new sleeper carriages have since been introduced in Europe.
Fares on busy night train routes can rise quickly, and getting new sleeper cars financed and approved is difficult.
Supporters say night trains need to become cheaper than flying to be a real alternative.
The emission figures are UK government conversion factors for 2022, in grams of CO2e per passenger-kilometer.
A domestic flight produces about 6.9 times the emissions per passenger-kilometer of UK national rail (245.87 vs 35.49 grams).
In 2019 more than 40 million passengers used Sweden's 10 Swedavia airports, down 4 percent from 42 million in 2018, a rare fall for a European country.
Swedavia gave several reasons for the fall in passengers: Sweden's aviation tax, worries about the economy, the weak Swedish crown and the climate debate.
